title: Sales Enablement: Comprehensive Playbook — Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pricing Guidance, Case Studies & Security FAQ
author: Jordan Lee
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook bundles the canonical positioning and messaging for Redwood Inference, short competitive briefs for outbound and AE prep, recommended pitch-deck structure, practical pricing guidance for early commercial conversations, two customer case studies with impact metrics, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ. Use this doc as the single source of truth for sales, solutions engineering, and marketing enablement.

Audience: AEs, SDRs, solutions engineers, sales engineering managers, and lifecycle sellers preparing enterprise conversations.

Quick summary bullets:
- Core positioning: Redwood is a developer-first inference platform that makes LLM-powered features predictable and economical across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Differentiators: production-grade runtime optimizations, unified deployment/ops experience (hosted / dedicated / private), cost-performance controls (batching, caching, quantization profiles), and enterprise SLAs + compliance options.
- Typical buyer personas: engineering-led PLG product teams, platform teams, and security/compliance-focused enterprise buyers.

1) Positioning & Messaging (One-pagers / Battlecards)

Core value proposition (elevator):
- For engineering teams building LLM features, Redwood Inference provides a unified runtime and orchestration that delivers predictable latency, reduced per-token cost, and enterprise controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — so teams ship faster and operate reliably without building complex inference infrastructure.

Three messaging pillars:
1. Production performance and reliability
   - 95th percentile P50/P95 latency SLAs, dedicated GPU pools, and automatic fallback policies reduce user-facing errors and keep apps running under load.
   - Talking points: "P95 latency targets, autoscaling for throughput spikes, fallbacks to compatible model variants."
2. Cost & operational control
   - Intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization guidance reduce per-token costs while maintaining output quality.
   - Talking points: "30–50% cost reductions typical after applying batching + caching; reserved capacity for predictable unit economics."
3. Deployment flexibility & compliance
   - Same API and tooling across hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC/on‑prem). Integrations for KMS/HSM, audit logs, and retention controls.
   - Talking points: "Pin model versions for rollouts, private control planes for regulated workloads."

Elevator scripts (short):
- 15s technical elevator: "Redwood gives engineering teams a single inference runtime that runs high-throughput LLM workloads with built-in batching, caching, and kernel optimizations — so you get predictable latency, lower per-token cost, and enterprise-grade controls without rewriting code for different deployments."
- 30s business elevator: "We help product teams ship LLM features faster with predictable costs and reliability. If you want the simplicity of an API but the controls of a private deployment, Redwood gives you a single way to operate across both."

Objection handling (concise):
- "Why not just use cloud model endpoints?" — Cloud endpoints often lack workload-aware batching, KV caching, and consistent SLAs across private deployments. Redwood focuses on inference economics and deployment parity for production apps.
- "We already have a self-hosted runtime." — Redwood reduces engineering overhead: unified routing, rollouts, observability, and model lifecycle tooling that typically cost months to build.

2) Competitive Briefs (short-form for call prep)

Competitors covered: OpenAI (hosted API), Anthropic, Cohere, Google Vertex AI / PaLM endpoints, AWS Bedrock/SageMaker endpoints, self-hosted runtimes (LLM infra vendors).

Comparison matrix (high level):
| Dimension | Redwood Inference | OpenAI / Anthropic | Cloud Endpoints (Vertex/Bedrock) | Self-hosted runtimes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Deployment modes | Hosted / Dedicated / Private | Hosted only | Hosted / managed | Private only |
| Production controls (SLA, rollouts) | Enterprise SLAs, rollouts, tracing | Limited to hosted | Varies; limited private parity | Varies; heavy engineering |
| Cost controls | Batching, caching, quant profiles | Usage-based only | Some autoscaling; limited batching | Depends on infra engineering |
| Observability | Token-level cost/latency, per-route dashboards | Basic usage metrics | Varies | Depends on instrumentation |
| Compliance & private deployment | VPC & on-prem with KMS/HSM integrations | Not available | Some enterprise options | Available but requires build |

Competitive positioning bullets (talking tracks):
- vs hosted-only APIs (OpenAI/Anthropic): Emphasize deterministic performance and private deployment parity — customers get the API simplicity but can graduate to dedicated or private without rewriting integrations.
- vs cloud-managed endpoints: Emphasize cost-reduction controls (prefix caching, continuous batching) and a higher degree of inference-specific optimizations and recommendations.
- vs self-hosted vendors: Emphasize productization — less engineering lift, observability, and SLAs out of the box.

Win themes (examples):
- Platform consolidation: teams with multiple model endpoints consolidate to one runtime to reduce variance in latency and observability.
- Cost predictability: teams moving from pure usage billing to a mix of reserved capacity + optimization reduce month-to-month cost volatility.
- Regulated workloads: customers needing VPC/on-prem + KMS integrations choose Redwood for compliance parity.

3) Pitch Deck Structure & Slide Guidance

Recommended 10–12 slide flow for AE decks:
1. Cover / 1-line value prop
2. Customer pain & evidence (latency, cost, ops burden)
3. Redwood overview & what we do (visual of hosted/dedicated/private)
4. How it works at a high level (runtime + orchestration + caching)
5. Key differentiators (3 bullets)
6. Pricing summary / deployment options
7. Security & compliance (private deployment, KMS, audit logs)
8. Observability & SLOs (dashboards, per-route metrics)
9. Case studies / results (2 short examples)
10. Typical onboarding & timeline (POCs, integration steps)
11. Pricing & procurement checklist
12. Next steps & ask (trial, technical discovery, SE workshop)

Slide tips for SEs:
- Use concrete numbers: latency P95, cost delta (%) from existing setup, typical onboarding lead times (2–6 weeks).
- Include a simple architecture diagram showing routing policy: hosted -> dedicated -> private fallback.
- Include a one-page tech appendix for SREs (SLOs, quotas, token accounting).

4) Pricing Guidance (talking points & sample ranges)

Guiding principles:
- Start commercial conversations with use-case sizing (monthly tokens, concurrency, retention needs).
- Recommend an evaluation path: 30–90 day POC on hosted with optional Dedicated pilot for predictable throughput.
- Use reserved capacity for customers needing predictable unit economics; combine with usage for burst.

Sample pricing constructs (indicative; final commercial quotes handled by pricing team):
- Hosted (self-serve / pay-as-you-go): usage-based pricing; example ballpark: $0.00X per 1K prompt tokens + $0.00Y per 1K completion tokens (refer to official pricing page for exact rates).
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): monthly commitment based on GPU type + reserved throughput. Example: small reserved pool (equiv. 2x A10G) $XXk/mo; medium (4x A100) $YYk/mo.
- Private / Enterprise: platform license + support tier + deployment services. Typical structure: one-time deployment fee, annual platform license tied to reserved capacity + support.

Discounting guidance:
- Early-stage startups: flexible terms for strategic references.
- Enterprise: multi-year committed reserved capacity for steeper discounts (~15–30% depending on commit).

Procurement checklist for AE & legal:
- Ask for desired deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Confirm data residency & retention requirements, KMS/HSM needs.
- Determine expected peak RPS and token volumes for sizing reserved capacity.
- Request standard SOC2 / ISO artifacts if requested.

5) Case Studies (two short wins to use in decks)

Case Study A — Conversational SaaS (PLG scale)
- Customer: "FastHelp" (SaaS knowledge-base + chat).
- Challenge: unpredictable latency at peak, rising per-token costs, inconsistent model versions between environments.
- Solution: Migrated from multi-vendor hosted endpoints to Redwood hosted with prefix caching and continuous batching; later moved to Dedicated pool for peak traffic.
- Results (90 days post-rollout): 40% reduction in P95 latency, 35% reduction in per-token operating cost, 99.95% platform uptime during business hours.
- Quote to use: "Redwood gave us predictable performance and cut our inference spend — our support SLAs finally stopped breaking during peak traffic." — Head of Engineering, FastHelp

Case Study B — Regulated Financial Services (Private)
- Customer: "CapitalBridge" (financial advisor platform).
- Challenge: strict data residency, audit trails, and HSM-backed key management; previous attempts to self-host added 6 months of engineering overhead.
- Solution: Private deployment (VPC) + KMS integration + audit logging; Redwood-managed control plane with on-prem inference nodes.
- Results (post-deployment): Compliance signoff in 8 weeks (instead of estimated 6 months), reduced engineering time-to-production by 60%, and achieved P95 latency 120ms in region during peak trading hours.
- Quote to use: "We retained full control of our keys and met audit requirements without rebuilding our inference pipeline." — Security Lead, CapitalBridge

6) Security FAQ (prospect-facing, brief answers)

Q: Where is customer data stored and processed?
A: Hosted workloads are processed in the region selected by the customer; we offer Dedicated and Private deployments for customers who require VPC or on-prem processing. Data retention policies are configurable per contract.

Q: How do you handle keys and encryption?
A: Redwood integrates with customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can support HSM-backed key stores for private/on‑prem deployments. All data in transit uses TLS 1.2+ and at-rest encryption is applied for hosted and private nodes.

Q: Do you provide audit logs and access controls?
A: Yes. We provide detailed audit logging, role-based access controls (RBAC), and integration with SSO providers (SAML/OIDC). Logs can be shipped to customer-managed sinks for long-term retention.

Q: Can we run Redwood entirely on-prem or air-gapped?
A: Yes — our Private offering includes an on-prem packaging option with an offline installation path and air-gapped deployment playbook. Professional services can assist with installation and validation.

Q: How do you ensure model output safety and guardrails?
A: Redwood supports evals and quality-guardrails integrated into the deployment pipeline, prompt filters, and post-processing hooks. We also support deployment-time model version pinning and automated regression detection against baseline prompt sets.

Q: What certifications and evidence can you provide?
A: We provide SOC 2 Type II reports and maintain an internal compliance program with documented evidence. For enterprise deals we coordinate evidence sharing under NDA as required.

7) Recommended SE/AE play for a typical discovery -> pilot -> procurement motion

Discovery (0–2 weeks):
1. Gather workload sizing: expected monthly tokens, average sequence length, concurrency, latency targets, and retention/compliance constraints.
2. Align on deployment mode for pilot (hosted or dedicated pilot) and security requirements.

Pilot (2–8 weeks):
1. Technical kickoff with SEs (1–2 days).
2. Ingest sample prompts / traffic profile; run baseline measurements vs current provider.
3. Apply batching/caching/quantization recommendations from Optimize team.
4. Measure P95 latency and per-token cost improvements.
5. Deliver pilot summary and recommended next steps (Dedicated sizing or Private deployment plan).

Procurement & Onboarding (4–12 weeks):
1. Legal & procurement review: standard SOW + SOC2 artifacts.
2. If Dedicated/Private: finalize topology, KMS integration, and rollout schedule.
3. SE-led cutover and post-launch monitoring plan (30–90 day health check).
